mainTopic: Handling and cutting on שבת and יום טוב: רבי נחמיה's view, and the משנה on making a lamp, charcoal, and cutting a wick
overview: The גמרא shows that שמואל's ruling about untying fastenings matches a ברייתא, then explains that the strict part of that ברייתא, about vessels on שבת, follows רבי נחמיה, who allows handling vessels only for their normal use. It challenges this from three ברייתות about burning vessels on יום טוב, one of which shows רבי נחמיה being strict on יום טוב too. It answers that two תנאים report רבי נחמיה's view differently. A new משנה then forbids shaping a clay lamp, making charcoal, and cutting a wick on יום טוב, while רבי יהודה allows cutting the wick with fire. רב יוסף traces the lamp rule to רבי מאיר, or in another version to רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק, and אביי's pushback is answered because an unfired lamp can hold coins. A ברייתא about חרניות pots is brought and the word is explained as villagers' bowls. The ban on charcoal is explained as charcoal for a bathhouse that day, in a case of sweating before the decree. The amud ends as the גמרא begins asking why a knife may not be used to cut a wick, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: שמואל follows a ברייתא about fastenings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that שמואל's ruling matches a ברייתא that treats fastenings on the ground differently from fastenings on a vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל ruled like this תנא, as a ברייתא teaches: fastenings attached to the ground may be untied, but not unraveled or cut, on both שבת and יום טוב. Fastenings on a vessel may be untied on שבת, but not unraveled or cut. On יום טוב they may be untied, unraveled and cut.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the earlier difficulty with שמואל's ruling by showing that a תנא in a ברייתא holds like him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא splits the cases into two groups: fastenings attached to the ground, like on a door, and fastenings on a vessel. For ground fastenings, untying is allowed on both days, which supports שמואל. For vessel fastenings, יום טוב is more lenient than שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Fastenings or seals, such as knotted ropes that close something
That are attached to the ground

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the three actions. Untying (מתיר) opens the knot. Unraveling (מפקיע) pulls the rope apart. Cutting (חותך) slices through it. The ברייתא allows different actions in different cases.

phrases.english: He spoke in accordance with this Tanna,
phrases.notes: "He" is שמואל, whose ruling the גמרא was just questioning.

phrases.english: as it is taught in a Baraisa:
Fastenings that are attached to the ground —
phrases.notes: For example, ropes tied on a door.

phrases.aramaic: מַתִּיר, אֲבָל לֹא מַפְקִיעַ וְלֹא חוֹתֵךְ,
phrases.english: one may untie them, but not unravel and not cut them,
both on Shabbos and on Yom Tov.
And those of a vessel —

phrases.aramaic: בְּשַׁבָּת מַתִּיר, אֲבָל לֹא מַפְקִיעַ וְלֹא חוֹתֵךְ,
phrases.english: on Shabbos one may untie, but not unravel and not cut;
on Yom Tov one may untie, unravel and cut.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty that the גמרא raised just before this section against שמואל's ruling.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the ruling follows a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל's ruling seemed to have no source among the תנאים.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל follows the תנא of this ברייתא, who allows untying fastenings attached to the ground.

steps.title: The second half of the ברייתא still contradicts שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the first half of the ברייתא supports שמואל, but the second half, about vessels on שבת, does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: You have explained the first part. But the last part is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back: the ברייתא only helps with part of שמואל's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רישא, about ground fastenings, fits שמואל. The סיפא forbids unraveling and cutting a vessel's fastenings on שבת, but שמואל allows unraveling in all cases. So the ברייתא now seems to go against him.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of a teaching
The last part of a teaching

phrases.english: You have explained for yourself the first clause,
but the latter clause is difficult!
phrases.notes: The latter clause is the part about a vessel on שבת, where unraveling is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּרֵצְתְּ לָךְ רֵישָׁא, אֶלָּא סֵיפָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 1 by using the other half of the same ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that שמואל follows the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא forbids unraveling a vessel's fastenings on שבת, while שמואל permits unraveling.

steps.title: The second half follows רבי נחמיה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the סיפא follows רבי נחמיה, who says vessels may only be handled for their normal use.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It is רבי נחמיה, who said: all vessels may only be handled for their normal use.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the strict part of the ברייתא comes from רבי נחמיה, so it does not have to bind שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The strictness on שבת is not about the rope itself. It comes from רבי נחמיה's rule about handling tools: a knife, for example, is normally used for food, not for cutting rope. Since this is רבי נחמיה's own view, שמואל does not have to follow it.

keyTerms.meaning: In the way they are normally used

steps.whyThisMatters: This connects the rope question to the wider laws of handling vessels on שבת (מוקצה and moving tools).

phrases.english: Whose view is this? It is Rabbi Nechemya,
who said: All vessels
may be handled only in the manner of their use.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the clause to an individual תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The סיפא seemed to be a general rule against שמואל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The סיפא follows רבי נחמיה's strict view on handling vessels, so it does not bind שמואל.

steps.title: Why would רבי נחמיה's rule apply only to שבת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if this is רבי נחמיה, his rule should apply on יום טוב too, not just on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is רבי נחמיה, why speak only about שבת? The same should be true even on יום טוב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 3. The ברייתא is lenient on יום טוב, but רבי נחמיה's rule should apply there as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rules about handling vessels are normally the same on שבת and יום טוב. So if the strictness comes from רבי נחמיה, the ברייתא should forbid it on יום טוב too. Yet it allows untying, unraveling and cutting on יום טוב.

phrases.english: If it is Rabbi Nechemya,
why specifically Shabbos?
It should be so even on Yom Tov as well!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה, מַאי אִירְיָא שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 3 by pointing to the יום טוב leniency in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: Assigning the סיפא to רבי נחמיה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי נחמיה's handling rule should apply on יום טוב as well, but the ברייתא is lenient on יום טוב.

steps.title: Does רבי נחמיה treat שבת and יום טוב differently?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings up a possible defense, that רבי נחמיה treats the two days differently, and questions whether that is really his view.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that רבי נחמיה makes a difference between a rabbinic rule of שבת and a rabbinic rule of יום טוב, does he really make such a difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא predicts how someone might defend the answer, and then casts doubt on that defense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One could try to say that for רבי נחמיה, the שבות rules of שבת and יום טוב are not the same. The גמרא doubts that he really holds this. In steps 6 and 7 it proves the doubt from three ברייתות, and step 8 gives the final answer.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different to him; he makes a distinction
A rabbinic restriction for the holy day

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא שַׁנְיָא לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה
phrases.english: And if you say there is a difference to Rabbi Nechemya

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין שְׁבוּת שַׁבָּת לִשְׁבוּת יוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: between a rabbinic restriction of Shabbos and a rabbinic restriction of Yom Tov,
does he really make a difference?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא שַׁנְיָא לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Blocks a possible answer to the challenge of step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The possible defense that רבי נחמיה treats שבת and יום טוב differently
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It is doubtful that רבי נחמיה makes any such distinction.

steps.title: Three conflicting teachings about burning vessels on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes three ברייתות that disagree about using vessels and broken pieces of vessels as fuel on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: But one ברייתא teaches: you may burn vessels but not broken pieces of vessels. Another teaches: you may burn both vessels and broken pieces. A third teaches: you may burn neither vessels nor broken pieces.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is challenging the idea from Step 5 that רבי נחמיה treats שבת and יום טוב differently. It sets up the challenge by quoting three ברייתות that seem to contradict each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three ברייתות are about יום טוב, and they give three different rulings. The third one forbids burning even whole vessels. In the next step the גמרא will show that this strict ruling comes from רבי נחמיה, which would mean his rule does apply on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: one may light a fire / use as fuel
but isn't it taught (opens a challenge from a ברייתא)

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in one ברייתא:
One may kindle a fire with vessels,
phrases.notes: All three teachings are about יום טוב, when lighting a fire for cooking is allowed.

phrases.english: but one may not kindle with broken pieces of vessels.
And another ברייתא teaches:

phrases.aramaic: מַסִּיקִין בֵּין בְּכֵלִים בֵּין בְּשִׁבְרֵי כֵּלִים,
phrases.english: One may kindle both with vessels and with broken pieces of vessels.
And yet another ברייתא teaches:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מַסִּיקִין לֹא בְּכֵלִים וְלֹא בְּשִׁבְרֵי כֵלִים.
phrases.english: One may kindle neither with vessels nor with broken pieces of vessels.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the defense raised in Step 5 that רבי נחמיה treats שבת and יום טוב differently.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי נחמיה limits vessels to their normal use only on שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא about יום טוב forbids burning even whole vessels, and that view will be identified as רבי נחמיה's.

steps.title: Each teaching follows a different תנא, and the strict one is רבי נחמיה
steps.stepSummary: The well-known solution assigns the three ברייתות to רבי יהודה, רבי שמעון, and רבי נחמיה, which shows רבי נחמיה forbids even on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is the standard answer: there is no problem. One teaching is רבי יהודה, one is רבי שמעון, and one is רבי נחמיה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the usual way of settling the three ברייתות. It uses that answer as proof that רבי נחמיה's strict rule applies on יום טוב too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה accepts מוקצה, so whole vessels are fine but broken pieces are not. רבי שמעון does not accept מוקצה, so both are allowed. רבי נחמיה forbids even whole vessels, since burning is not their normal use, and this ruling is about יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: and it is answered (the standard solution)
it is not difficult; there is no contradiction
items set aside, not to be handled on שבת or יום טוב

steps.confusionAlert: This step is not the גמרא's final answer. It is the proof that makes Step 5's defense hard to keep. The real answer comes in the next step.

phrases.english: And it is answered: it is not difficult,
this one follows רבי יהודה,
this one follows רבי שמעון,
and this one follows רבי נחמיה!
phrases.notes: This is the third teaching, which forbids even whole vessels on יום טוב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge from Step 6 by naming which תנא each ברייתא follows.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי נחמיה forbids non-standard use of vessels even on יום טוב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The accepted resolution of the three ברייתות, which assigns the ruling that forbids even whole vessels to רבי נחמיה.

steps.title: Two תנאים report רבי נחמיה's view differently
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that two later תנאים disagree about what רבי נחמיה held: one says his rule covers יום טוב too, and the other says only שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are two תנאים, each explaining the view of רבי נחמיה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It says there is a disagreement about how to report רבי נחמיה's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both תנאים agree that רבי נחמיה allows vessels only for their normal use. One reports that he applies this on יום טוב as well, which is the third ברייתא. The other reports that he applies it only on שבת, which matches the סיפא from Step 3, so the explanation from that step still holds.

keyTerms.meaning: according to / explaining the view of

steps.whatToRemember: Two תנאים disagree about רבי נחמיה. Everyone agrees he limits vessels to their normal use, but they disagree whether this applies on יום טוב or only on שבת. This saves the explanation that the סיפא follows רבי נחמיה.

phrases.english: These are two תנאים
who disagree about the view of רבי נחמיה.
phrases.notes: Literally 'according to רבי נחמיה.' Each one reports his opinion differently: one says only on שבת, the other says on יום טוב too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the proof of Step 7 by splitting the reports of רבי נחמיה's opinion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Disagreement among later תנאים about what an earlier תנא held
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because one ברייתא shows רבי נחמיה forbidding on יום טוב, it seemed the סיפא, which applies only to שבת, could not follow him.
steps.terutzMaskana: A different תנא reports רבי נחמיה as limiting the rule to שבת, and the סיפא follows that report.

steps.title: New משנה: no making a lamp, charcoal, or cutting a wick on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The משנה forbids shaping a clay lamp, making charcoal, and cutting a wick on יום טוב, and רבי יהודה allows cutting the wick with fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: On יום טוב one may not hollow out clay to make a lamp, because that is making a vessel. One may not make charcoal on יום טוב, and one may not cut the wick. רבי יהודה says: he may cut it by burning it in the fire.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists three things you may not do on יום טוב, and רבי יהודה gives one exception about the wick.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making a lamp means creating a new vessel, which is not allowed. Making charcoal is not part of preparing food for the day. Cutting a wick is like fixing up a vessel, but רבי יהודה allows shortening it with fire. The גמרא asks in step 25 why fire is different from a knife.

keyTerms.meaning: hollowing out (shaping clay into a lamp)

phrases.english: משנה:
One may not hollow out a lamp,
phrases.notes: He means pressing a hollow into a lump of clay so it can hold oil and a wick.

phrases.english: because he is making a vessel.
And one may not make charcoal on יום טוב.
And one may not cut the wick.
רבי יהודה says:
He may cut it with fire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On יום טוב one may not shape a clay lamp, make charcoal, or cut a wick. רבי יהודה permits shortening the wick by burning it.

steps.title: Who holds that hollowing a lamp makes a vessel?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds that hollowing out a clay lamp counts as making a כלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Who is the תנא who holds that hollowing out a lamp makes a vessel?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה by asking which תנא is behind the rule that hollowing out a lamp makes a כלי. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lamp has only been shaped. It has not been fired in a furnace yet. The גמרא wants to know who holds that a clay item counts as a כלי at that early stage, because not everyone would agree.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא (who taught this)?

phrases.english: GEMARA: Who is the tanna who taught
phrases.notes: This goes back to the משנה in step 9, which forbade shaping a clay lamp on יום טוב.

phrases.english: that hollowing out a lamp makes a vessel?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה quoted in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that a shaped but unfired clay lamp counts as a כלי.

steps.title: רב יוסף: It is רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the משנה follows רבי מאיר, who holds that a clay vessel can become טמא once its shaping is finished, even before firing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: It is רבי מאיר. A ברייתא teaches: From when can a clay vessel become טמא? From when its work is finished. This is רבי מאיר's view. רבי יהושע says: From when it is fired in the furnace.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers that the משנה follows רבי מאיר. He proves it from a ברייתא about when a clay vessel can become טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that a clay vessel counts as a כלי once it is shaped, so it can become טמא even before firing. That fits the משנה, which treats shaping a lamp as making a כלי. רבי יהושע requires firing, so by his view hollowing the lamp would not yet make a vessel.

keyTerms.meaning: A furnace or kiln for firing clay

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: רַבִּי מֵאִיר הִיא.
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: It is Rabbi Meir.
As it is taught: An earthenware vessel,
from when can it become impure?
From when its work is finished; these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
phrases.notes: Finished here means shaped into its final form, even though it has not been fired yet.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says: From when it is fired in the furnace.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב יוסף רבי מאיר היא דתניא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי מאיר, who holds that a shaped but unfired clay vessel already counts as a כלי.

steps.title: אביי: A lamp may be different from a regular vessel
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that רבי מאיר may count an unfired vessel only because it can hold things, while an unfired lamp seems useless.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: How do you know? Maybe רבי מאיר said this only there, because a vessel can hold something. But here, what is the lamp good for?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רב יוסף's proof. He suggests that רבי מאיר's rule might not apply to a lamp.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's reason could be that an unfired pot is already useful, since it can hold dry things. An unfired lamp cannot hold oil or burn properly, so it may not be useful at all. If so, the ברייתא does not prove that רבי מאיר would call a hollowed lamp a כלי.

keyTerms.meaning: He only said this until here (only in that case)

phrases.english: Abaye said to him: From where do you know?

phrases.aramaic: דִּלְמָא עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר הָתָם
phrases.english: Perhaps Rabbi Meir only said it there
because it is fit to hold something in it,
but here, what is it fit for?
phrases.notes: Here means the unfired lamp from our משנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ליה אביי ממאי דלמא עד כאן לא קאמר רבי מאיר התם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof brought in step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from רבי מאיר, not the משנה's rule.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: An unfired pot is useful, while an unfired lamp may not be, so the two cases might not be comparable.

steps.title: The lamp can hold coins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that an unfired lamp is also useful, since it can hold small coins.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is fit to hold small coins in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers אביי's question. An unfired lamp is useful after all, because coins can be kept in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's distinction depended on the lamp being useless. Since it can hold coins, it is just like the unfired pot. So רבי מאיר's view can still stand behind the משנה.

phrases.english: To hold small coins in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the case fits the original reason
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An unfired lamp is useless, so רבי מאיר might not count it as a כלי.
steps.terutzMaskana: An unfired lamp can hold coins, so it is useful like any unfired vessel, and רבי מאיר's view applies.
steps.whatToRemember: By the first version, the משנה follows רבי מאיר: a shaped clay item that has some use already counts as a כלי, even before firing.

steps.title: Second version: It is רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק
steps.stepSummary: In another version, רב יוסף says the משנה follows רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רב יוסף said: It is רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of רב יוסף's answer. In this version he names a different תנא, and the proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This version names רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק as the source instead of רבי מאיר. The proof is a משנה about unfinished pots (step 15). אביי raises the same pushback against it (steps 16–17).

phrases.english: Some say: Rav Yosef said:
It is Rabbi Eliezer, son of Rabbi Tzadok,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another answer to the question of step 10, replacing steps 11-13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק.

steps.title: Proof from the חרניות pots
steps.stepSummary: A משנה about unfinished pots shows that רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק treats a clay item as a vessel once its work is finished.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: חרניות pots are pure regarding the impurity of a tent over a dead body, and impure regarding carrying by a זב. רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק says: They are pure even regarding carrying by a זב, because their work is not finished.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה that proves the second version. רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק calls these pots pure because their work is not finished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reason is only that the pots are unfinished, not that they were never fired. That suggests that once the shaping is finished, they count as vessels even before firing. That matches the משנה's view that shaping a lamp makes a כלי.

keyTerms.meaning: A type of unfinished clay pot
Impurity spread by being under one roof with a dead body
Impurity passed on when a זב carries or moves an item

steps.whatToRemember: By the second version, the משנה follows רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק, who makes the key point whether the item's work is finished, not whether it was fired.

phrases.english: As we learned: Haraniyyot pots,
are pure regarding a tent over a corpse,
and impure through carrying by a zav.
Rabbi Eliezer, son of Rabbi Tzadok, says:
They are pure even through carrying by a zav,
because their work is not finished.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the proof for the attribution made in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה about the lamp follows רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about חרניות pots, where his only reason is that their work is not finished.

steps.title: אביי pushes back on the proof from רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק may call the unfinished pots vessels only because they can hold things. An unfired lamp seems useless.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Maybe רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק only said this there, because those pots can hold something. But here, what is a lamp good for?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on the second version of רב יוסף's answer. This is the same kind of challenge he raised earlier against the רבי מאיר version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof in step 15 showed that רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק counts unfired pots as vessels. אביי says the reason may be that pots can actually hold things. If so, the rule might not cover an unfired lamp, which seems to have no use.

keyTerms.meaning: he only said his view up to this point (in that case)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a mistake or a needless repeat. The גמרא is running the same challenge and answer from steps 12–13 again, this time against the second version, which names רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Perhaps he only stated his view
Rabbi Eliezer son of Rabbi Tzadok, there,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the case of the unfinished pots from the previous step.

phrases.english: because it is fit to hold something in it,
but here, what is it fit for?
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the unfired lamp from our משנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: דִּלְמָא עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 15
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the unfinished pots to the unfired lamp
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Pots can hold things, but an unfired lamp seems useless, so the two cases may differ

steps.title: The unfired lamp can hold small coins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that an unfired lamp is useful too, because it can hold small coins.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is good for holding small coins.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers אביי the same way it did before: the lamp has a use, because coins can be kept in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's whole challenge depended on the lamp being useless. Once it has a real use, it is like the pots, so the proof from רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק stands.
steps.whatToRemember: In both versions, רבי מאיר and רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק, an unfired clay item counts as a vessel once its shaping is finished. An unfired lamp qualifies because it can hold small coins.

phrases.english: To hold small coins in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's pushback
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows a real use, so the challenge falls away
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An unfired lamp is useless, so it is not a vessel
steps.terutzMaskana: It can hold coins, so it counts as a vessel

steps.title: A ברייתא on hollowing a lamp and making חרניות pots
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that on יום טוב one may not hollow out a lamp or make חרניות pots. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל permits the pots.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: One may not hollow out a lamp, and one may not make חרניות pots on יום טוב. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל permits making חרניות pots.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא on the same topic as our משנה: shaping clay items on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא forbids both hollowing a lamp and making these pots. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagrees only about the חרניות pots. The גמרא next explains what חרניות are.

keyTerms.meaning: a type of simple pot (explained next)

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One may not hollow out a lamp,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין עוֹשִׂין אִלְפָּסִין חִרָנִיּוֹת בְּיוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: and one may not make ḥaraniyyot pots on a Festival.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel
permits making ḥaraniyyot pots.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין פּוֹחֲתִין אֶת הַנֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a related ברייתא on shaping clay items on יום טוב
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא forbids hollowing a lamp and making חרניות pots on יום טוב; רבן שמעון בן גמליאל permits the pots

steps.title: What are חרניות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what חרניות are. רב יהודה says they are ערניות.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are חרניות? רב יהודה said: ערניות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the unusual word in the ברייתא means. רב יהודה swaps it for a related word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה reads חרניות as ערניות, a word connected to עיר, a town. That word also needs explaining, which sets up the next step.

phrases.english: What are ḥaraniyyot?
Rav Yehuda said: iraniyyot.
phrases.notes: He swaps the ח for an ע, so the word becomes connected to עיר, a town.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains a word in the ברייתא

steps.title: What are ערניות? Villagers' bowls
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what ערניות are. אביי says they are villagers' bowls.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are ערניות? אביי said: bowls used by villagers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a clearer meaning of רב יהודה's word. אביי explains that these are simple bowls that villagers use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Simple villagers do not mind using rough, half-finished clay bowls. So making such bowls counts as making a usable vessel, and that is why the תנא קמא forbids it on יום טוב.

phrases.english: What are iraniyyot?
Abaye said: villagers' bowls.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains רב יהודה's word further

steps.title: Why does the משנה need to forbid making charcoal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ban on making charcoal and asks why it needs saying, since charcoal seems to have no יום טוב use.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'And one may not make charcoal.' But that is obvious. What is it good for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the next line of the משנה. It challenges the line as unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום טוב, only work needed for food and similar needs is allowed. Making charcoal does not seem to serve any such need, so the ban looks too obvious to state. The גמרא wants to find a case where someone might have thought it was permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: it is obvious (a challenge that the line is unneeded)

phrases.english: And one may not make charcoal.
That is obvious; what is it fit for?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ban on making charcoal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Charcoal has no יום טוב use, so the ban seems needless

steps.title: רבי חייא: charcoal for the bathhouse that same day
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא explains that the ban is needed for charcoal given to bathhouse attendants to heat the bath that same day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא taught: It is needed only for giving the charcoal to bathhouse attendants for use that same day.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא gives a case where charcoal does have a יום טוב use: heating a bathhouse that day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think that charcoal used that day for washing counts as a יום טוב need, and so making it would be allowed. The משנה teaches that it is still forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: it was needed only for (this case)

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya taught:
It was needed only
to hand them over to bathhouse attendants for that same day.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא: לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a specific case where the ban teaches something new
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Charcoal for that day's bath is a יום טוב need, so making it is allowed
steps.terutzMaskana: Making charcoal is forbidden even then

steps.title: Is bathing even allowed on that day?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי חייא: is heating a bathhouse for use on יום טוב allowed at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: And on that same day, is it allowed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי חייא's case. Using a bathhouse on יום טוב itself seems forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Rabbis forbade bathing in a bathhouse on יום טוב. If so, nobody would think the charcoal serves a permitted need, and רבי חייא's case seems to fall apart.

phrases.english: And on that same day, is it permitted?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי חייא's case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Bathing on יום טוב is forbidden, so there would be no reason to think making the charcoal is allowed

steps.title: Using רבא's answer: sweating, before the decree
steps.stepSummary: Using רבא's explanation from elsewhere, the גמרא says the case is entering the bathhouse only to sweat, at a time before the decree against sweating.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבא said: it is about sweating, and before the decree. Here too: it is about sweating, and before the decree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא borrows רבא's answer from another discussion and applies it here to save רבי חייא's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on bathing does not cover just sitting in the bathhouse to sweat. Sweating was later forbidden too, but before that decree it was allowed. So רבי חייא's case is someone who went in to sweat before the decree. Then the charcoal really served a permitted need, and the משנה still forbids making it.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's ban on making charcoal teaches something new. Even when the charcoal heats a bathhouse for permitted sweating (before the decree), making it is still forbidden on יום טוב.

phrases.english: As Rava said:
to sweat, and before the decree.
Here too:
to sweat, and before the decree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רבי חייא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the case to sweating, at a time before the decree
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי חייא's case involves forbidden bathing
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is permitted sweating before the decree, so רבי חייא's explanation stands

steps.title: Why may a wick not be cut with a knife?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling against cutting a wick into two on יום טוב. It then begins asking why cutting with a knife is forbidden when רבי יהודה allows cutting with fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: "And one may not cut a wick into two." What is different about a knife, that one may not cut with it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה about cutting a wick. It then starts a question that sets up the next move: what is the difference between a knife and fire?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה forbids cutting a wick in two, but רבי יהודה allows cutting it with fire. Both methods leave you with two shorter wicks, so the גמרא wants to know why the knife is treated more strictly. The question breaks off here, and the explanation comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: what is different? (asks what makes one case unlike another)

steps.confusionAlert: The quoted line only shows the ban. The comparison to fire comes from רבי יהודה's view in the משנה, which allows cutting with fire. That is why the גמרא asks about the knife in particular.

phrases.english: And one may not cut the wick into two.
What is different about a knife, that one may not [cut with it]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the discussion of making charcoal (Steps 21-24), the גמרא moves to the next clause of the משנה, about cutting a wick.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the reason that cutting a wick with a knife is forbidden, while רבי יהודה permits cutting it with fire?
